description.narrative:
Project Ogbin (from the Nigerian Yoruba word ogbin meaning agriculture) is a youth led agribusiness launchpad in Ibadan, Nigeria that equips young people, especially young women in rural and peri urban communities who are not in education, employment or training (NEET), with practical income-generating green skills through a low cost greenhouse farming model. The project combines hands-on training, mentorship and youth leadership opportunities to support participants to move into dignified green jobs andyouth owned agribusinesses, while contributing to climateâ€‘resilient food production and local economic development in their communities
Goal: Empower marginalized youth (18-35), especially young women NEET in rural and peri urban Oyo, with practicalgreen skills, leadership, and entrepreneurship in climate-resilient agriculture through a low-cost greenhouse model over 12 months.
Objectives: Train 60 NEET youth (60% young women) in greenhouse production, business, and leadership, supporting >30 totransition into paid roles or green micro-enterprises; construct 6 low-cost greenhouses as training hubs and revenue-generating units.
Activities: Manually recruit youth andsecure host community land; train youth on greenhouse farming and agribusiness from construction to market; construct, plant, and sell from 6 greenhouses.

participating-org.narrative: Eco Science Generation (EcoSciGen) is a youth-led not-for-profit social enterprise dedicated to providing actionable solutions to the climate crisis by empowering communities and individuals with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to shape a climate-resilient future. We believe that effective climate action begins with those most affected by climate change, which is why we work closely with vulnerable people <(>&<)> communities to enhance adaptive capacity, improve livelihoods, and strengthen resilience against climaterisks. Our core objective is to empower 103,500 Nigerian youth to become climate leaders and solution-builders within their communities, while supporting 210 marginalized communities to strengthen their resilience to climate and socio-economic challenges through locally driven, inclusive interventions by 2030. Our mission is to provide actionable solutions to the climate crisis through youth <(>&<)> community empowerment, education and leadership development. We are guided by some important key core values, which includesempathy, respect, excellence, creativity,community, and teamwork, as we strive to generate meaningful impact while building a collaborative platform where every member's unique contributions advance our vision of a truly climate-resilient world (truly to us meansclimate resilience that is lived, inclusive, community-owned,and sustained beyond projects or policies, where people have the agency and resources to adapt and thrive). As a youth-led organization, we take time to understand local contexts and the interconnected challenges young people face, including how climate impacts exacerbate poverty, unemployment, and limited access to quality education. Our interventions are intentionally designed to be sustainable, to tap into the strengths, knowledge, and resources within communities, and to contribute to transformational and long-term resilience for both individuals and communities.
